newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Maracaibo pilot strike threat continues.
newsitem.headline: Maracaibo pilot strike threat continues.

text.p: A strike threat by pilots who guide oil tankers in and out of Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo through a narrow canal continues, but pilots' representative Fidel Sanchez told Reuters a strike would be a last resort.
"The idea is not to strike -- unless we have to -- but raise the issue (of the state of the canal) nationally," Sanchez said.

Sanchez said the pilots had decided Tuesday to file a strike petition as a way of pressuring authorities to improve conditions in the channel. The channel, which ships some 1.5 million barrels daily, has seen three tankers run aground in the past two months.
Under Venezuelan law, workers can only strike 120 hours after filing a petition with the Labor Ministry.
"We want the draught limit on boats reduced to 36 feet from the current 38 feet while dredging of the channel continues," said Rodriguez.

The channel's normal 39.5 foot limit was tightened to 36 feet in March after the Nissos Amorgos and Olympic Sponsor ran aground in the space of two weeks -- but the limit was subsequently eased to 38 feet.

Rodgriguez added that the pilots would be meeting Thursday with representatives from the National Canal Authorities and the Ministry of Transport and Communications to discuss the state of the canal, as well as the pilots' demands.
